alex_j: Hey people-ops — planning a 4-week workcation in Lisbon in June. Keeping my US homebase (NY). Do I need to submit anything for WFH stipend eligibility or payroll? Also worried about tax nexus / benefits while I'm away.

people_ops: Thanks for the heads up, Alex. Short answer: yes please submit the travel notification form and the temporary remote request. For a 4-week (<=30 days) stay we usually treat it as temporary remote — stipend eligibility stays the same but we need the paperwork.

alex_j: ok cool — what paperwork exactly? link?

people_ops: 1) Travel notification (link to internal form) — includes dates and location. 2) Temporary remote approval — manager sign-off. 3) Confirm that you'll keep homebase as NY. If homebase doesn't change we don't move payroll.

miguel_g: Quick add — if you're in Portugal >90 days we escalate to legal for tax nexus review. Under 90 days, standard policy says team members remain on their payroll country. But confirm with payroll before booking long non-refundable travel.

alex_j: So no change to benefits or health coverage for 4 weeks?

emily_hr: Correct — benefits remain on plan tied to your homebase while you're traveling short-term. Medical/network coverage doesn't move for <=30 days. If you extend beyond 90 days we need to review local requirements and open an international payroll conversation.

ben_engine: FYI — we ask folks to keep working overlapping hours with their team. For Lisbon that’s ~5 hour difference with NY, so plan for some late afternoons. Not a policy blocker but helpful to mention in your manager approval.

alex_j: Re: WFH stipend — still get the monthly allowance even if I'm traveling? Prorated?

people_ops: Good question. For single-month travel that doesn’t change your regular monthly stipend. We only prorate when homebase changes mid-pay-period or if you change employment status. Example: moving homebase mid-month triggers proration.

alex_j: Any travel reimbursements for coworking or wifi while on workcation?

people_ops: We don't reimburse personal travel or lodging. If you expect to need coworking for official team meetings, submit a one-off expense request with receipts and manager justification. Routine cafe wifi or coworking for personal preference isn't covered.

alex_j: Tax forms? Should I expect withholding differences while abroad?

people_ops: Since payroll remains in the US for <=30 days, withholding doesn't change. If you switch homebase or exceed the 90-day threshold then payroll/legal will reach out about withholding and potential local registration.

alex_j: Anything else I should be aware of?

people_ops: A few small operational things:
- update your Slack status with local hours and timezone
- set OOO/working hours on calendar if shifted
- confirm emergency contact info and local address in Workday (optional)

people_ops: Please cc your manager on the travel notification. Once we receive it payroll will confirm no action needed for a 4-week stay. If legal needs to review (rare for <=30 days) we'll loop you in.

alex_j: thanks! submitting now.

hr-bot: Reminder: submit travel-notification form — https://redwood.internal/forms/travel-notification — auto-reminder in 48h if not completed. :paperclip:

alex_j: Submitted the form and added my manager. Ping me if you need anything else.

people_ops: Got it, saw the submission. You'll get a confirmation email from payroll by EOD tomorrow. Enjoy Lisbon! :sun_with_face:
